messages:
support-bot: :rotating_light: Alerts started 10:12 UTC — p99 latency for /v1/generate jumped from ~450ms to ~1.8s after the runtime rollout. Alert link: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/alerts/runtime-p99 (incidents/INC-4921 created).
maya: which rollout? host/region?
support-bot: Canary rollout of runtime v2.3.1 -> started ~08:40 UTC, 10% traffic. Affected: hosted-us-west1-primary. Sample request_id=req_7f9b2c. Repro steps included below.
sanjay: copying. Can someone paste a flamegraph/trace for that request_id? Is this consistent across models or only certain seq lengths?
support-bot: Trace: https://jaeger.redwood.company/trace/req_7f9b2c. Quick metrics: p95 from 220ms->820ms, p99 from 450ms->1.8s, tail tokens spiked. Affected requests skew to longer prompt lengths (>800 tokens).
leo: saw the alert too. Traffic split shows majority of affected requests are served by canary nodes with image runtime:v2.3.1. Old nodes (v2.3.0) show normal latency.
irene: oncall here — have we tried switching canary back to v2.3.0? Minimal blast radius for rollback.
sanjay: before rollback let's triage a bit — suspects: (1) new continuous-batching heuristic, (2) kernel-selection tweaks that prefer a different matmul kernel for sequences >512, (3) an updated cuda driver pinned in the image. If we can toggle config flags on the canary nodes to disable continuous batching that should be fast to test.
maya: how do we flip the flag? Isn't batching config baked into the runtime args?
sanjay: we have a runtime configmap. command:```kubectl -n hosted patch configmap runtime-config --patch '{"data":{"continuous_batching":"false"}}'``` then rolling restart daemonset runtime-canary. Or to pin image:```kubectl -n hosted set image ds/runtime-canary runtime=redwood/runtime:v2.3.0``` (this will fully rollback canary).
irene: I'm fine rolling back the canary to stop user impact while y'all debug — doing set image now.
deploy-bot: Canary canary-rollout for runtime:v2.3.1 -> 10% traffic started by @deploy-bot at 2026-03-15T08:40:12Z.
deploy-bot: Image update triggered: set image ds/runtime-canary runtime=redwood/runtime:v2.3.0 by @irene at 2026-03-15T10:20:03Z.
maya: after rollback, we should monitor p99 for 10 minutes then re-open canary with narrower changes.
(small pause)
leo: quick check: 2 minutes after rollback p99 down to ~480ms, p95 ~230ms — back to baseline. Good to confirm rollback worked.
sanjay: ok rollback confirms regression is in v2.3.1. Next: we need to bisect the change set. I have a suspected commit range: 9f3a2c -> b7c21d (inference batching + kernel selection). I'll run a local bisect job against the synthetic load harness targeting longer sequences.
maya: can we reproduce in staging? I can spin up a staging canary with v2.3.1 and enable synthetic traffic that mimics >800 token prompts. Command I use:```loadgen --endpoint https://staging-hosted.redwood/api/v1/generate --concurrency 50 --median-prompt-length 900 --duration 600s --header 'Authorization: Bearer ${STAGING_KEY}'```
sanjay: good. If staging reproduces, we'll try toggling two flags independently: continuous_batching and kernel_heuristic. Patch configmap keys:```continuous_batching: false
kernel_heuristic: legacy```. That should tell us if the batching change or kernel selection is dominant.
maya: running loadgen now in staging. Will report in 12 minutes.
(some minutes)
maya: staging load shows similar p99 spike with v2.3.1. I toggled continuous_batching=false on staging canary — p99 dropped ~35% immediately.
sanjay: that strongly implicates the continuous-batching heuristic. There was a change that tries to batch aggressively for long sequences which increases head-of-line blocking in some cases.
leo: do we want a short-term mitigation on hosted? Either keep canary rolled back (current) or enable continuous_batching=false across canary nodes and re-roll. Which is less risky?
irene: current rollback is lowest risk; but we should be able to re-introduce v2.3.1 with continuous_batching disabled to validate other fixes.
sanjay: plan: 1) keep rollback live (done). 2) Run bisect on commits to isolate the exact patch; I already queued bisect job CID=bisect-177900. 3) If bisect isolates batching commit, prepare a patch to revert or gate it behind a config flag defaulting off. 4) Once patch ready, do small canary with continuous_batching=false. 5) Roll forward with monitoring thresholds.
maya: also add a temporary rule in the routing layer to limit request size for canary to <1200 tokens to reduce risk while we test.
leo: I've opened tracking PR #PR-1214 to gate the heuristic behind a runtime flag, and INC-4921 will track customer impact + postmortem.
sanjay: for engineers working on the bisect, here's the bisect command I used locally:```git bisect start b7c21d 9f3a2c
# iterate by building images: docker build -t redwood/runtime:bisect-$GIT_SHA .
# push image and run loadtest against a staging instance
```
maya: taking notes in postmortem doc: https://docs.redwood.company/postmortems/INC-4921 (will populate root cause, timeline, tests).
irene: final status: canary rolled back to v2.3.0, customer-facing latency restored. Owners: sanjay->bisect + fix, maya->staging repro + load tests, leo->PR + coordination, irene->incident commander. ETA for patch: 24-48h.
sanjay: quick follow up: add an e2e test in CI that runs a short long-seq load test to prevent this regression. I'll open a follow-up ticket.
maya: thanks everyone. leaving monitoring on until 11:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Incident INC-4921 status updated: mitigated (canary rollback).
